name: Kedorlaomer
title: King of Elam
summary: Kedorlaomer was the king of Elam who led a coalition of four kings from Mesopotamia. He had subjugated five kings in the Jordan Valley for twelve years, but when they revolted, he waged war against them and captured among others Lot, Abraham's nephew. He was finally defeated by Abraham in a daring night attack.

keyEvents.title: Kedorlaomer's dominion over the Jordan Valley
keyEvents.description: Kedorlaomer had ruled over the five kings in the Valley of Siddim for twelve years, including the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah.

keyEvents.title: The Rebellion of the Five Kings
keyEvents.description: In the thirteenth year, the five kings in the Jordan Valley rebelled against Kedorlaomer's dominion.

keyEvents.title: Kedorlaomer's Campaign
keyEvents.description: In the fourteenth year, Kedorlaomer and his three allied kings launched a major military campaign, defeating several peoples, including the Rephaites, Zuzites, Emim, and Horites.

keyEvents.title: The Battle in the Valley of Siddim
keyEvents.description: Kedorlaomer and his allies defeated the five kings in the Valley of Siddim. The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, and the victors plundered the cities.

keyEvents.title: Lot Taken Captive
keyEvents.description: During the plundering of Sodom, Kedorlaomer's forces captured Lot, Abraham's nephew, along with his possessions.

keyEvents.title: Abraham's Victory over Kedorlaomer
keyEvents.description: When Abraham heard that Lot had been taken captive, he gathered 318 of his trained men and pursued Kedorlaomer all the way to Dan. In a night attack, Abraham defeated Kedorlaomer and his allies, freeing Lot and recovering all the plunder.
